## Part 3 - The role of factor orders in visualizations

Now that you have a `season` variable, you can compute and visualize summaries for each season in the same manner as in previous milestones. Run the chunk below to view a summary table.

```{python}
#| label: 'summary'

seasons_summary = (covid
  .groupby(['season'])
  .agg({'deaths': 'sum'})
  .rename(columns={'deaths': 'total_deaths'})
  .reset_index()
)

seasons_summary
```

After you have run the chunk above to create `seasons_summary`, run the chunk below to visualize the data of `seasons_summary`.

```{python}
#| label: 'summary_plot'

from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_col, labs

p1 = (
  ggplot(seasons_summary, aes(x='season', y='total_deaths'))
  + geom_col()
  + labs(title='COVID-19 deaths by season')
)
p1.show()
```

This is a nice plot, but the order of seasons on the x axis is arbitrary (alphabetical). We may want to give the seasons a more principled order before we publish this plot.
